_meta.indication: Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture, defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, or multiple risk factors for fracture; or patients who have failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy.
_meta.receipt_date: Original BLA dated and received December 19, 2008

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.population: Postmenopausal women aged 60 to 91 years (mean 72) with a baseline BMD T-score between -2.5 and -4.0 at the lumbar spine or total hip
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: incidence of new morphometric (radiologically-diagnosed) vertebral fractures at 3 years
pivotal_trials.result: New vertebral fracture incidence at year 3 was 7.2% (placebo) vs 2.3% (Prolia); absolute risk reduction 4.8%, relative risk reduction 68% (p < 0.0001). Hip fracture 1.2% vs 0.7%, RRR 40% (p = 0.04). Nonvertebral fracture 8.0% vs 6.5%, RRR 20% (p = 0.01).

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Evaluate Denosumab in the Treatment of Postmenopausal Osteoporosis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5% and more common than placebo): back pain (34.7% vs 34.6%), pain in extremity (11.7% vs 11.1%), hypercholesterolemia (7.2% vs 6.1%), musculoskeletal pain (7.6% vs 7.5%), and cystitis (5.9% vs 5.8%). Serious nonfatal infections were more frequent with Prolia (4.0%) than placebo (3.3%).
target_moa: Denosumab is a human IgG2 monoclonal antibody that binds RANKL, preventing it from activating its receptor RANK on osteoclasts and their precursors; this inhibits osteoclast formation, function, and survival, decreasing bone resorption.

rems.type: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure benefits outweigh the risks of serious infection including skin infection, dermatologic adverse events, and over-suppression of bone turnover.

advisory_committee.vote: The Reproductive Health Drugs Advisory Committee met August 13, 2009 and voted unanimously in favor of approval of denosumab for treatment (but not prevention) of postmenopausal osteoporosis.

summary.text: Prolia (denosumab), the first monoclonal antibody submitted for treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis, was submitted as a BLA on December 19, 2008; after an August 13, 2009 Advisory Committee that recommended approval for treatment, FDA issued a Complete Response letter on October 16, 2009, and the drug was approved following a Complete Response resubmission with a required REMS and multiple postmarketing requirements.

This submission is a Complete Response to the October 16, 2009, action letter issued for the biologic licensing application (BLA) for denosumab (Prolia). Denosumab is a human-monoclonal IgG2 antibody that targets receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B ligand (RANKL).

An Advisory Committee meeting was convened on August 13, 2009 to discuss all 4 indications. With regard to osteoporosis, the committee recommended approval for treatment (BLA 125,320) but not prevention (BLA 125,331). requirement.text: A retrospective cohort study using multiple existing observational databases to assess background rates of serious infection including skin infection, dermatologic adverse events, and over-suppression of bone turnover in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis.

citations.quote: 1. A retrospective cohort study using multiple existing observational databases to collect data from a 5-year period prior to the availability of denosumab. The study should identify women with postmenopausal osteoporosis and determine the occurrence of serious infection including skin infection, dermatologic adverse events, and over-suppression of bone turnover in each database in order to assess the background rates of those adverse events. The data obtained in this study will be used to inform the implementation of postmarketing requirement #2. The final protocol for this study was submitted on January 25, 2010.

requirement.text: A long-term observational study in administrative databases to prospectively evaluate the incidence of serious infection including skin infection, dermatologic adverse events, and over-suppression of bone turnover in postmenopausal women administered Prolia.

citations.quote: The data obtained in this study will be used to inform the implementation of postmarketing requirement #2. The final protocol for this study was submitted on January 25, 2010.

basis.text: CR action was based on lack of full agreement on product labeling and postmarketing activities, with a determination that a REMS was necessary and long-term postmarketing studies would be required to address serious infections, dermatologic adverse events, and over-suppression of bone turnover.

citations.quote: After consultations between the Office of New Drugs and the Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology, it was determined that a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) would be necessary to ensure that the benefits of denosumab outweigh the risks. In addition, long-term postmarketing studies would be required.
